nodes.name: Chlorine-doped Ni(OH)₂ electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: Well-organized Cl-Ni(OH)₂ was deposited in situ on conductive substrates by a facile electrochemical deposition by introducing the charged terminal Cl⁻ anion from NaCl (5 mM), which acted as a structural support and electric field regulator. The SEM image exhibits more evenly distributed nanoflowers and ordered structure.
nodes.source_text: Originally, well-organized Cl-Ni(OH)₂ was deposited in situ on conductive substrates by a facile electrochemical deposition by introducing the charged terminal Cl⁻ anion from NaCl... With the addition of a chlorine ion, the SEM image of Cl-Ni(OH)₂ exhibits the more evenly distributed nanoflowers...

nodes.name: Chlorine electrochemical etching
nodes.procedure: Cl-Ni(OH)₂ nanoflower precursor shown in Fig. 2(d) transforms into a loose and porous EE/Cl-Ni(OH)₂ flower-like particle with a smaller size of ~100 nm via a flexible electrochemical refactoring process at 0.4 V, which will provide ample channels for ion transport.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pristine Ni(OH)₂ shows irregular clustered nanoparticles of 200-500 nm; Cl-Ni(OH)₂ shows evenly distributed nanoflowers; EE/Cl-Ni(OH)₂ shows loose porous flower-like particles ~100 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The scanning electron microscopy (SEM) images exhibit the structure and morphology of as-prepared products in Fig. 2.

nodes.characterization_summary: EE/Cl-Ni(OH)₂ nanoflower consists of interlaced ultrathin films; longitudinally distributed ultrathin nanosheets with thickness ~2.1 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The TEM image in Fig. 2(f) again reveals that EE/Cl-Ni(OH)₂ nanoflower consists of interlaced ultrathin film on the edge.

nodes.characterization_summary: EE/Ni(OH)₂ shows low crystallinity with small crystalline grains; lattice distance of 0.2334 nm corresponding to (101) plane of Ni(OH)₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The observed lattice distance of 0.2334 nm is referring to the (101) lattice plane of Ni(OH)₂ shown in the high-resolution TEM (HR-TEM) image in Fig. 2(i).

nodes.characterization_summary: EMPA mapping shows Ni, O, Cl uniformly distributed in EE/Cl-Ni(OH)₂ lattice; Cl content decreases after electrochemical etching.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The electron microprobe analysis (EMPA) mapping images in Fig. 2(e) indicate that the content of Cl element decreases after selectively electrochemical etching.

nodes.characterization_summary: Chlorine content decreases from 0.32 at% to 0.23 at% after electrochemical treatment.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Similarly, the result of energy dispersive spectrometer (EDS) in Table S1 shows that the chlorine element in the structure decreases from 0.32 at% to 0.23 at% after electrochemical treatment.

nodes.characterization_summary: Elemental mapping confirms uniform Ni, O, Cl distribution in EE/Ni(OH)₂ nanosheet.
nodes.evidence_snippet: (j) Field-emission scanning electron microscopy with energy dispersive spectrometer (FESEM-EDS) elemental mappings of Ni, O, and Cl of EE/Ni(OH)₂ nanosheet.

nodes.characterization_summary: All samples match β-Ni(OH)₂ (JCPDS NO 14-0117); Cl-Ni(OH)₂ shows (001) and (100) peaks shifted to smaller angles indicating larger layer spacing; EE samples show weakened peaks due to defects.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As presented in Fig. 3(a), every characteristic peak of pure Ni(OH)₂ and Cl-Ni(OH)₂ could be accurately matched with the β-Ni(OH)₂ (JCPDS. NO 14-0117).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni-O stretching vibrations at 310 cm⁻¹ (A₁g(T)) and 460 cm⁻¹ (E_g(T)); Cl-Ni(OH)₂ shows shift to higher wavenumber and Ni-Cl at 374 cm⁻¹; EE/Cl-Ni(OH)₂ shows redshift of E_g(T) peak.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 3(e), the two conspicuous peaks centered on 310 and 460 cm⁻¹ referring to the A₁g(T) and E_g(T) phonons can be ascribed to the stretching vibration of the Ni–O bond.

nodes.characterization_summary: O 1s peaks at 530.2 eV (O_L), 531.0 eV (O_V), 532.5 eV (O_W); O_V ratio increases from 16.5% in Cl-Ni(OH)₂ to 23.5% in EE/Cl-Ni(OH)₂; Ni 2p peaks shift negatively with Cl doping.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Particularly, the O 1s XPS spectra exist in three bonding environments according to the actual condition at 530.2, 531.0, and 532.5 eV in Fig. 2(g) and Fig. S2(b-e).

nodes.characterization_summary: EE/Cl-Ni(OH)₂ and Cl-Ni(OH)₂ show strong signal at g=2.003 indicating abundant oxygen vacancies.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In comparison with pristine Ni(OH)₂, Cl-Ni(OH)₂ and EE/Cl-Ni(OH)₂ exhibit a remarkable EPR signal at g = 2.003, revealing the presence of affluent oxygen deficiency in the lattice.

nodes.characterization_summary: Double-layer capacitance C_dl = 1.47 mF cm⁻² for EE/Cl-Ni(OH)₂ (vs 0.56 mF cm⁻² for pristine Ni(OH)₂ and 0.84 mF cm⁻² for Cl-Ni(OH)₂), indicating significantly higher ECSA.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The calculated C_dl value of Cl-Ni(OH)₂ (0.84 mF cm⁻²) is obviously larger than that of pure Ni(OH)₂ (~0.56 mF cm⁻²). Surprisingly, under an applied electric field, the C_dl value of EE/Cl-Ni(OH)₂ dramatically increases to 1.47 mF cm⁻², which is more than twice as large as pure Ni(OH)₂.
